units.title: Minimum unit-radius lamps on a three-point diagonal strip
units.statement: Let A be the lattice points (x,y) with 0≤x,y≤n and |x−y|≤1. A radius strictly between 1 and sqrt(2) covers precisely the selected point and its horizontal or vertical neighbors. The minimum number of lamps placed at A to cover A is n+1. All n+1 diagonal points suffice. Any solution can be transformed without adding lamps to one supported only on the diagonal: a pair of off-diagonal lamps between consecutive diagonal points can be replaced by both endpoints; any remaining single off-diagonal lamp can be replaced by its uncovered diagonal endpoint or removed. Then every diagonal point needs its own lamp.
steps: View the strip as consecutive diagonal vertices with two off-diagonal points between each pair
Replace both off-diagonal lamps on an edge by its two diagonal endpoints
Replace any remaining off-diagonal lamp by the still-unlit endpoint, then count all diagonal points
